$comment: Canonical identifiers for the published Chinese proficiency standards. See spec/README.md. Registry version is the date it last changed.

hsk-2012.$note: Level 1-6. Superseded for grading purposes but still the basis of a great deal of published material.

gf0025-2021.name_zh: 国际中文教育中文水平等级标准
gf0025-2021.name_en: Chinese Proficiency Grading Standards for International Chinese Language Education
gf0025-2021.issuer: Ministry of Education of the PRC and State Language Commission
gf0025-2021.$note: A national GRADING STANDARD, not an examination syllabus. Levels 7, 8 and 9 are one undifferentiated band. This is the document almost every open dataset encodes.

hsk-syllabus-2025.name_zh: 中文水平考试HSK考试大纲
hsk-syllabus-2025.name_en: Syllabus for the Chinese Proficiency Test
hsk-syllabus-2025.issuer: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (中外语言交流合作中心)
hsk-syllabus-2025.$note: The EXAMINATION SYLLABUS. Shares the name 'HSK 3.0' with gf0025-2021 and assigns a different level to 41.5% of the vocabulary the two share. Distributed as a 406-page PDF. Published word count counts entries; homographs graded at two levels appear more than once.

tbcl-2025.name_en: Taiwan Benchmarks for the Chinese Language
tbcl-2025.issuer: National Academy for Educational Research (國家教育研究院)
tbcl-2025.$note: Levels 1 to 4 each appear in two forms, 第N級 and 第N*級; both belong to their numbered level. Filtering on the unstarred form discards 442 of 3,100 characters, 1,398 of 14,452 words, and 212 of 496 grammar points -- 43% of the grammar inventory. The three inventories are NOT parallel: characters and words run to level 7, grammar stops at level 5. Levels 1 and 2 sit below CEFR A1 in listening, reading and writing. NAER asserts rights over the lists.

tocfl-8000-2024.issuer: Steering Committee for the Test of Proficiency-Huayu (國家華語測驗推動工作委員會)
tocfl-8000-2024.$note: The one Chinese framework carrying an official CEFR correspondence. Novice 1 and 2 sit below A1 by design. SC-TOP asserts rights over the list.

$ambiguous_names.$note: The reason this registry exists. A dataset labelled 'HSK 3.0' names one of two documents that disagree about 41.5% of shared vocabulary, and the label does not say which.
